text.tspan: Hands cultivate a garden with care.
A community garden needs more than seeds and tools. Our neighbourhood project showed that sharing responsibility and
communicating clearly help people work well together.
First, dividing the work gives everyone a way to contribute. We started small: two neighbours brought tools, while others
bought seeds. We also worked out a watering schedule so that the garden was never just one person’s responsibility.
Second, clear communication helps a group solve problems. When someone forgot to water the plants, we checked the
schedule together. We made the instructions clearer instead of blaming the person, so everyone could follow through.
The garden taught us two useful lessons: share the work fairly and discuss problems openly. These habits helped our plants
grow and made us a stronger team. Other community projects can benefit from the same approach.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Persuade a group to change how they care for a plant. Support your recommendation with two different reasons and a
practical example of each. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One
possible outline: introduce the situation; discuss observing a plant helps us respond to what it needs with an example; discuss
keeping a simple record helps us learn from changes with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
